title: Maps on cohomology of modules induced by f-maps (pullback, edge map)
statement: Let $h:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal G$ an $\mathcal O_Y$-module and $\mathcal F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $\varphi:\mathcal G\to h_*\mathcal F$ a morphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules, $h_*$ the direct image, $(h_*\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(h^{-1}V)$ (an *$h$-map* from $\mathcal G$ to $\mathcal F$; equivalently, by the adjunction $h^*\dashv h_*$ [def-pc-module-pullback], a morphism $h^*\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$). For $p\ge0$ the map $\varphi^*:H^p(Y,\mathcal G)\to H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ between the cohomology groups of [pqf-def-cohomology] is defined as follows. Choose injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions] $s_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules and $s_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to\mathcal J^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules, with $\mathcal I^n=\mathcal J^n=0$ for $n<0$, so that $H^p(X,\mathcal F)=H^p(\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet))$ and $H^p(Y,\mathcal G)=H^p(\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J^\bullet))$; choose a cochain complex [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] $\mathcal J'^\bullet$ of injective $\mathcal O_Y$-modules with $\mathcal J'^n=0$ for $n<0$ and a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] $\lambda:h_*\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal J'^\bullet$, $h_*$ applied termwise; and choose a morphism of complexes $\beta:\mathcal J^\bullet\to\mathcal J'^\bullet$ with $\beta^0\circ s_{\mathcal G}=\lambda^0\circ h_*(s_{\mathcal F})\circ\varphi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal J'^0$. Since $\Gamma(Y,h_*\mathcal I^n)=\mathcal I^n(h^{-1}Y)=\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^n)$, $\Gamma(Y,\lambda)$ is a morphism of complexes $\mu:\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet)\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J'^\bullet)$, and $\mu$ is a quasi-isomorphism (proof, Step 4). Then $\varphi^*=H^p(\mu)^{-1}\circ H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta))$. Names: (a) the *pullback* $h^*:H^p(Y,\mathcal G)\to H^p(X,h^*\mathcal G)$ is $\varphi^*$ for the unit $\varphi=\eta_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to h_*h^*\mathcal G$ of $h^*\dashv h_*$; (b) for an open $U\subseteq Y$, with $j:U\to Y$ the inclusion of the open subscheme and $\mathcal G|_U$ the restricted $\mathcal O_U$-module, $(\mathcal G|_U)(V)=\mathcal G(V)$ for $V\subseteq U$ open [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], the *restriction* $\mathrm{res}^Y_U:H^p(Y,\mathcal G)\to H^p(U,\mathcal G|_U)$ is $\varphi^*$ for the $j$-map $\rho_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to j_*(\mathcal G|_U)$ whose component on an open $V\subseteq Y$ is the restriction map $\mathcal G(V)\to\mathcal G(V\cap U)$; (c) the *edge map* $e_{h,\mathcal F}:H^p(Y,h_*\mathcal F)\to H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ is $\varphi^*$ for $\varphi=\mathrm{id}_{h_*\mathcal F}$. (That $\varphi^*$ does not depend on the choices, is $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$-linear, is $\varphi_Y$ in degree $0$, is $H^p(\varphi)$ for $h=\mathrm{id}_Y$, and that $\mathrm{res}^Y_U$ is the pullback $j^*$ up to $j^*\mathcal G\cong\mathcal G|_U$, are statements about this definition, recorded in `pointers`.)

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Section 01F7 (section-functoriality): Lemma 01F8 (lemma-functoriality), Equations 01F9/01FA (equation-functorial-derived, equation-functorial) and Remark 01FB (remark-explain-arrow), with Lemma 01EZ (lemma-before-Leray) for the quasi-isomorphism

proof.text: *The choices exist.* $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ and $\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)$ have enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-complex-injective-resolution-mono] with $a=0$ to the complex $\mathcal F[0]$ ($\mathcal F$ in degree $0$) gives a complex $\mathcal I^\bullet$ of injectives with $\mathcal I^n=0$ for $n<0$ and a quasi-isomorphism $\mathcal F[0]\to\mathcal I^\bullet$, i.e. $0\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^0\to\mathcal I^1\to\cdots$ exact: an injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions]; likewise $\mathcal G\to\mathcal J^\bullet$. The direct image $h_*$ is an additive functor $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)\to\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)$ [def-pc-module-pullback], so $h_*\mathcal I^\bullet$ (termwise, $h_*(d)$ as differentials, $h_*(d)h_*(d)=h_*(dd)=0$) is a cochain complex with $h_*\mathcal I^n=0$ for $n<0$, and [lem-weil-pbc-complex-injective-resolution-mono] with $a=0$ gives $\lambda:h_*\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal J'^\bullet$, a quasi-isomorphism into a complex of injectives vanishing in negative degrees.

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Remark 01FB (remark-explain-arrow): 'Choose a resolution $\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ by a complex of injective $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Choose resolutions $\mathcal G\to\mathcal J^\bullet$ and $f_*\mathcal I^\bullet\to(\mathcal J')^\bullet$ by complexes of injective $\mathcal O_Y$-modules'; existence by Injectives Lemma 01DI and Derived Categories Lemma 013K (3)

proof.text: *$\beta$ exists and is unique up to homotopy.* Let $K^\bullet=\mathcal G[0]$ and $\alpha:K^\bullet\to\mathcal J^\bullet$ the augmentation ($\alpha^0=s_{\mathcal G}$). It is a quasi-isomorphism (the augmented complex is exact) and a monomorphism in every degree ($s_{\mathcal G}$ is injective by exactness at $\mathcal G$, and $\alpha^n:0\to\mathcal J^n$ for $n\ne0$). Let $\gamma:K^\bullet\to\mathcal J'^\bullet$ be the morphism of complexes with $\gamma^0=\lambda^0\circ h_*(s_{\mathcal F})\circ\varphi$ (a morphism of complexes since $d_{\mathcal J'}\lambda^0h_*(s_{\mathcal F})=\lambda^1h_*(d_{\mathcal I}s_{\mathcal F})=0$). By [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso] there is $\beta:\mathcal J^\bullet\to\mathcal J'^\bullet$ with $\beta\circ\alpha=\gamma$, i.e. $\beta^0\circ s_{\mathcal G}=\lambda^0\circ h_*(s_{\mathcal F})\circ\varphi$. Two such $\beta_1,\beta_2$ satisfy $\beta_1\alpha=\beta_2\alpha$, so they are chain-homotopic by [lem-weil-pbc-lift-to-injective-unique-up-to-homotopy] ($\mathcal J'^\bullet$ bounded below of injectives); hence $H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta))$ does not depend on the choice of $\beta$ ($\Gamma(Y,-)$ is additive and carries homotopies to homotopies).

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Remark 01FB (remark-explain-arrow): 'By Derived Categories, Lemma 013P there exists a map of complexes $\beta$ such that the diagram (equation-choice) commutes'; uniqueness up to homotopy: literature/stacks-project/derived.tex Lemma 013S (lemma-morphisms-equal-up-to-homotopy)

proof.text: *$\mu$ is a morphism of complexes.* For each $n$, $\Gamma(Y,h_*\mathcal I^n)=(h_*\mathcal I^n)(Y)=\mathcal I^n(h^{-1}(Y))=\mathcal I^n(X)=\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^n)$ by the definition of the direct image [def-pc-module-pullback], and the differential $\Gamma(Y,h_*d^n)=(h_*d^n)_Y=d^n_X$ is that of $\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet)$; so $\mu^n=\lambda^n_Y$ defines a morphism of complexes $\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet)\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J'^\bullet)$, $\Gamma(Y,-)$ applied to the morphism of complexes $\lambda$.

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Remark 01FB (remark-explain-arrow): the equality $\Gamma(Y,f_*\mathcal I^\bullet)=\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet)$ in the second diagram; Remark 01F0 (remark-elucidate-lemma): 'the trivial observation that $\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet)=\Gamma(Y,f_*\mathcal I^\bullet)$'

proof.text: *$\mu$ is a quasi-isomorphism, so $\varphi^*$ is defined.* By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pushforward-injectives-sections-quasi-iso] (applied to $\mathcal I^\bullet$, $\mathcal J'^\bullet$, $\lambda$) $\mu=\Gamma(Y,\lambda)$ is a quasi-isomorphism, so $H^p(\mu):H^p(X,\mathcal F)=H^p(\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet))\to H^p(\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J'^\bullet))$ is a bijective homomorphism of abelian groups and has an inverse; with Step 2, $\varphi^*=H^p(\mu)^{-1}\circ H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta))$ is a well-defined homomorphism $H^p(\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J^\bullet))=H^p(Y,\mathcal G)\to H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ for the chosen resolutions $\mathcal I^\bullet,\mathcal J^\bullet,\mathcal J'^\bullet,\lambda$.

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Remark 01FB (remark-explain-arrow): 'The vertical arrow is a quasi-isomorphism by Lemma 01EZ ... The arrow is given by the composition of the horizontal map by the inverse of the vertical map'; Equation 01FA (equation-functorial)

proof.text: *The named $h$-maps are morphisms of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules.* (a) The unit $\eta_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to h_*h^*\mathcal G$ of the adjunction $h^*\dashv h_*$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is a morphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules. (b) For $U\subseteq Y$ open, $(j_*(\mathcal G|_U))(V)=(\mathcal G|_U)(j^{-1}V)=\mathcal G(V\cap U)$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], [def-pc-module-pullback]; the restriction maps $\rho_V:\mathcal G(V)\to\mathcal G(V\cap U)$ are $\mathcal O_Y(V)$-linear ($\mathcal O_Y(V)$ acting on $\mathcal G(V\cap U)$ through $\mathcal O_Y(V)\to\mathcal O_Y(V\cap U)$, the module axiom of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]) and commute with restriction along $V'\subseteq V$ (both composites are the restriction $\mathcal G(V)\to\mathcal G(V'\cap U)$), so $\rho_{\mathcal G}$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules. (c) $\mathrm{id}_{h_*\mathcal F}$ is one. So the three names are instances of the construction.
